source_read: PMC HTML (PMC3071736, author manuscript; Addiction 2010;105:1809-1818): structured abstract, Introduction, Methods (participants, in-patient milieu, MAWQ with Table 2, other procedures, data analysis), Results (demographics with Table 1, withdrawal symptoms, depressive symptoms, craving, craving-depression correlation, psychiatric symptoms) with Figure 1-4 legends, Discussion (all six subsections incl. limitations), acknowledgments, declarations of interest. Figures are images; values read from text and legends only.

claims.overstatement: Minor. 'In 56 people' is the number enrolled; the entry percentages come from the 32 with rater-scored MAWQ data, depressive scores from 28, craving from 26 and BSI ratings from 25, and later weeks come from a smaller, unreported subset (participants were in 2- or 5-week imaging studies). 'Most symptoms fell during the first one to two weeks' holds for the self-report BSI and BDI; on the rater-scored MAWQ only 8 of 30 items changed significantly over days 1-14 (the MAWQ craving item did not, p=0.79). The claim is more accurate than the paper's abstract, which says depressive and psychotic symptoms 'resolve within 1 week'.
claims.note: All numbers reproduce: 23/32 = 72%, 22/32 = 68.75% (printed 68), 20/32 = 63%, 18/32 = 56%; BDI above controls through week 3 (p<0.05 after adjustment), week 4 p=0.07; VAS craving lower than entry from week 2 (p<0.01) and present to week 5. Population: non-treatment-seeking, no other dependence or Axis I disorder, inpatients on a cue-restricted research ward compared with outpatient controls who differed in education, ethnicity, smoking (91% vs 45%), unemployment and parole status.

anchors.locator: Methods > MAWQ, Table 2 (n=32); Results > Methamphetamine withdrawal symptoms
anchors.extracted: At entry: 'often think about taking methamphetamine' 23 (72%), craving 22 (68%), increased appetite 20 (63%), tired/low energy 18 (56%), restless 13 (40%), no motivation 12 (38%); suicidal thoughts 2 (6%); feeling watched/talked about 3 (9%); hearing voices 1 (3%); being touched 1 (3%). Mixed-model time effects over days 1-14 significant for red/itchy eyes, no motivation, increased appetite, sleep difficulties, tiredness, feeling watched/talked about (p=0.009), thinking about methamphetamine (p=0.02), reduced sexual pleasure; not for the craving item (p=0.79) or the depressed item (p=0.26). Authors: symptoms mild; substantial changes occurred within 14 days.

BDI (28 users vs 89 controls): users' entry mean about 12 (mild-moderate); fell over first 2 weeks (time p<0.001); higher than controls through the first 3 weeks after adjustment for differing demographic/behavioural variables (p<0.05); approached controls only at end of week 4 (p=0.07).

anchors.locator: Results > Craving for MA; Figure 2 legend
anchors.extracted: VAS craving (n=26) elevated at entry and through week 1; lower than entry after 2 weeks (p<0.01 at each later time point) and continuing at a reduced level to week 5.

BSI (25 users vs 85 controls): most indices elevated at entry except phobia; fell in week 1 and reached a low baseline by end of week 2; time effects psychoticism p=0.003, paranoia p=0.003, depression p=0.001, GSI p<0.001; additional symptoms p=0.131, phobia p=0.506. Text says all subscales reached control levels by week 2 except 'additional symptoms', but also that users scored higher than controls at most time points.

anchors.locator: Methods > Participants, In-patient milieu; Discussion > Limitations
anchors.extracted: Users not seeking treatment, not dependent on other substances, no other current Axis I disorder; resident on a cue-restricted research ward with daily urine and breath tests, enrolled in 2- or 5-week imaging studies; controls outpatients. Authors: findings may not generalize to treatment-seeking users; inpatient vs outpatient setting may confound; no data beyond 5 weeks; rater-scored MAWQ gave lower intensities than self-report.

reporting_issues.note: Found independently; F about 35-50 for plausible group splits.
Recomputed: chi-square 31.3 (29.3 with continuity correction) for 40/89 vs 51/56; age F(1,111)=2.4 gives p=0.12.
Figure 3 legend: study entry = days 0-1 of abstinence; Methods: last use within 7 days before admission; Figure 4 legend: weeks of hospitalization.
True, but this is a limitation of the reading, not a reporting issue in the paper; it belongs in source_read. Reader 2 also did not extract figure values.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: one-week resolution in the abstract versus three weeks above controls for BDI; relapse-vulnerability claim without relapse data.
